Also fires accidentally on any branch not named exactly after its spec, including slashed names.

title: A recorded audit pass is never checked against the diff being merged
deliverable: check --merge refuses when the latest pass head is not an ancestor of HEAD, naming how many commits have landed since the audit.
evidence: cmdAudit computes base and head from git specifically to pin the reviewed range; checkMergeGate reads only verdicts and pass number. Audit once, then land any amount of unaudited code, and the gate stays green. Rule 2 says the audit reads a diff; nothing verifies which diff.

title: spec add promotes a pass-2 finding, bypassing rule 6
deliverable: spec add refuses a finding whose source pass is 2 or later, with the same message triage gives, and the test asserting the current permissive behaviour is inverted.
evidence: triage refuses to promote a finding whose source pass is 2 or later. cmdSpecAdd applies no guard on kind, state or source pass, and a test asserts that as intended behaviour. Proof clause 4 says a second pass cannot produce new work that blocks the merge; a documented verb does exactly that.

title: Proof clause 3 promises the store records who declined a finding, and no such field exists
deliverable: Either the Task record grows a who field that decline and triage populate, or proof clause 3 is amended to promise only what the store holds. Decide which before implementing.
evidence: The Task interface has reason and closed (a date) and no actor field of any kind. Measured against the live store: 104 declined, 104 carrying a reason, 0 carrying any author or who field. Pass 1 graded the clause met citing the reason-iff-declined rule, which covers why and is silent on who.
reason: Resolved by amending clause 3 rather than by adding a field: the store records why and when, and git records who changed it. Inventing an actor field to satisfy a sentence is the wrong direction when the commit already carries it.

title: tasks check stack-traces instead of reporting on a conflicted or malformed store
deliverable: loadStore reports a parse or shape failure as a check error naming the file and line number, instead of throwing an uncaught SyntaxError or TypeError.
evidence: loadStore does a bare JSON.parse per line with no line number, file name or shape validation. A store carrying git conflict markers dies with SyntaxError; a row missing requires dies with TypeError from inside checkStore. The design sells JSONL on merging clean, so the unclean case is the one that needs a readable failure, and it lands on the CI step named check.

title: The stale-file warning cannot see a path that was deleted and recreated with new contents
deliverable: check warns when a listed path was deleted and recreated since the task was written, not only when it is absent. Cheapest form: compare against the commit the task was created in.
evidence: checkStore warns only when a listed path no longer exists. scripts/tasks.ts did not exist on main; this branch created a new 948-line file at the predecessor tool path. Two open findings still carry line references into the old file (pass3-h1 and pass3-h2) and tasks check reports them as fresh.

title: lastAuditDoc is dead data that six manifest entries still keep correct by hand
deliverable: lastAuditDoc is removed from systems.json, scripts/lib/systems.ts and the three test fixtures, since nothing reads it.
evidence: audit-status dropped its documented() check on this branch. The field survives as one type declaration with zero production readers, six hand-maintained values in systems.json, and three test fixtures. CLAUDE.md forbids systems required to be manually kept in sync, and the spec decision an audit is a recorded pass, not a document, is what removed the reader.

title: No verb lists the store, so every deferred task is unreachable
deliverable: tasks list prints the store with filters for state, severity, system, spec and deferred, so an agent or a human can see open work that is not in the current spec.
evidence: fixNowQueue filters on spec equality and cmdNext refuses when there is no active spec, so the 51 open tasks carrying spec null cannot be reached by any command. backlog.md was 868 readable lines before this branch deleted it. CLAUDE.md points a cold session at tasks next, which returns nothing on main.

title: A deliverable understood better after implementation can only be changed by splitting the branch
deliverable: tasks spec amend copies the current Deliverable verbatim into an Amendments section with a date and a reason, lets the new text stand, and the gate compares against the last amendment. Changing a deliverable stays loud and stays in git, without splitting the branch.
evidence: The Deliverable section freezes when the branch opens and the only sanctioned change is closing the spec and opening another. There is no recorded-amendment path, so a requirement learned during implementation has nowhere to go except unfrozen prose or a branch split. Clause 2 was in fact reinterpreted in the unfrozen Decisions section one commit before the audit that graded it.

title: Cold resume returns nothing when the branch name and the spec filename disagree
deliverable: When docs/specs/BRANCH.md is absent and exactly one spec has open members, currentSpec resolves to it and says so. A cold session gets the right answer instead of silence.
evidence: currentSpec is existsSync of docs/specs/BRANCH.md and nothing else. This branch ran five commits with the spec at docs/specs/task-system.md while the branch was task-system-v2, during which next, handoff and check --merge all silently returned nothing. A cold agent in that window gets no spec, no queue and no signal that anything is wrong.

title: Rule 7 tasks name no files, so handoff points a cold session at nothing
deliverable: audit accepts --file against a proof clause, and the undelivered task it creates carries those paths, so handoff names where the next session should start.
evidence: cmdAudit hardcodes files as empty on every undelivered task, and --file attaches only to --finding, never to a proof clause. Proof clause 6 promises handoff names the files the next session needs; the only open task on this branch prints with no files line at all.

title: The store cannot be searched by topic, so a bundle has no query
deliverable: Half delivered: tasks search <term> matches id, title, system, deliverable and evidence, case-insensitively, and ANDs with every list filter. What remains is grouping. Text search finds 9 of the roadmap's combat tasks but misses runtime-2026-07-30-m2 and m3, which are about combat and never say the word - a bundle is a curated set, not a substring. Decide between a tags array and leaving the bundles as prose in .planning/.scratch.md.
evidence: There is no topic, epic or tag field, and no free-text query. Asking for everything to do with combat is currently a manual read of the roadmap in .planning/.scratch.md cross-referenced against tasks list, and the roadmap bundles exist only as prose. Two shapes were raised: a tags array on the Task record, or a tasks search command over the text a task already carries.
reason: Resolved by this spec's decision: keep text search and use specs as curated bundles rather than adding tags here.

title: Decide how much the handoff contract should guarantee
deliverable: A recorded decision on which of those seven guarantees are worth enforcing and which are deliberately left to prose, with any accepted ones implemented. The default answer may well be none of them: handoff already composes from four sources, so hardening the commit message alone would add gates without adding resumability. Decide before adding any check.
evidence: The commit-msg hook checks that a body and a Next: line exist, and nothing more. It does not guarantee that the body carries enough context, that Next: names an existing task, that it names files, that it matches the open queue, that the newest usable Next: is not stale, that exempt or --no-verify commits carry any handoff at all, or that CI validates message quality. A commit message is therefore a breadcrumb rather than a durable contract. The composition that actually carries a handoff is the latest Next: plus the spec deliverable plus the open fix-now list plus each task files, evidence and deliverable — which is what tasks handoff already assembles. The commit message must never be the only place the next agent learns what to do.

title: Amending a clause orphans its undelivered task
deliverable: A proof clause carries an identity that survives both rewording and reordering, so an undelivered task stays bound to its clause across an amendment. Either spec amend repoints existing undelivered tasks as part of the amendment, or clauses get a stable id that verdicts and task ids reference instead of text or position.
evidence: cmdDone matches an undelivered task's stored deliverable against the spec's current proof clauses to find its verdict. spec amend rewrites clause text, so the task is orphaned and refuses to close: task-system-v2-clause-1 is undelivered but its clause text no longer matches any proof clause. Hit for real while closing clause 1 on this branch; the workaround was tasks edit to repoint it by hand. Matching by ordinal index instead has the mirror-image defect the pass-1 audit already noted - inserting a clause silently rebinds every recorded verdict and every slug-clause-N id.

title: A [cN] tag is load-bearing identity but sits outside the deliverable freeze
deliverable: The freeze covers clause identity as well as clause prose, and duplicate or renumbered tags are refused by tasks check and the merge gate, not only by tasks audit. Today a prose-preserving tag edit is invisible to both.
evidence: In a scratch fixture, audit --proof 1=unmet --proof 2=met made the gate refuse with 'proof clause 1 is unmet as of pass 1'. Hand-editing that clause's tag from [c1] to [c2], prose untouched, made the line disappear: checkMergeGate walks clauses to verdicts and never verdicts to clauses, so a verdict whose clause id no longer exists is never read. tasks check reports 0 errors against a spec with two clauses tagged [c1]. Swapping [c1] and [c2] between two clauses passes check --merge with 0 issues while the recorded '- proof N:' lines now name different prose. The duplicate guard at tasks.ts:1164 is correctly sequenced within cmdAudit and is reached by the interactive walk, but it is the only place the invariant holds.

title: An undelivered task whose clause an amendment deletes can be neither done nor declined, and no command repoints it
deliverable: Dropping a proof clause through the sanctioned spec amend path leaves a closable task: either audit retires the undelivered task whose clause the amendment removed, or a command repoints it, so the branch is not left permanently unmergeable with hand-editing docs/tasks.jsonl as the only exit.
evidence: Sanctioned workflow only, no hand-editing: audit clause 1 unmet, delete the clause, spec amend, re-audit. done refuses with 'proof clause 1 is no longer in ...', decline refuses with 'undelivered and cannot be declined', and check --merge refuses forever on 'member(s) neither done nor declined'. The only exit is hand-editing docs/tasks.jsonl. Pre-existing on main, where clause-text matching deadlocked identically, so narrowed by this branch rather than introduced.
reason: We will only consider this once the event actually occurs.

title: The first stamp can silently rebind verdicts recorded before tags existed
deliverable: A reader can tell which clause an old "- proof N:" line named: passes recorded under ordinal identity are either migrated when the spec is stamped or marked as predating the tags.
evidence: Simulated against a spec whose pass 1 recorded proof 1/2/3 under ordinal identity: deleting clause B before the first stamp leaves the survivors stamped [c1] [c2], so pass 1's '- proof 2: unmet - B did not hold' now sits beside a c2 that is old clause C. Inherited from ordinal identity rather than introduced, but stamping is the moment identity freezes and nothing marks which passes predate it. The real docs/specs/task-system-v2.md is unaffected: its clauses 7-8 were appended, not inserted.
reason: This type of bulletproofing is not necessary for the system at the moment.

title: stampClauseIds writes ids into nested sub-bullets, hardening a parse quirk into recorded identity
deliverable: Only a top-level bullet under Proof: is a clause, so an indented sub-point stays prose instead of being rewritten into the document with an id a verdict can name.
evidence: A '  - sub-point' indented under a clause is scanned as a clause of its own, because scanProofClauses matches '- ' against the trimmed line, and stampClauseIds then rewrites it into the document as '  - [c2] sub-point'. The mis-parse predates this branch; what is new is that the tool now writes the id into the human's document and lets a verdict name it. No spec under docs/specs/ currently uses a sub-bullet under Proof:, so nothing is mis-tagged today.

title: New comments restate a test and describe other modules contracts
deliverable: The four comments added carry only facts their own file owns: the id-allocation rule lives in its test and in resolveIds, and the freezes rationale lives with the freeze in mergeGate.ts.
evidence: ProofClause.id's 'the lowest id no tag has claimed, in document order' is verbatim the name of its own test in specDoc.test.ts. stripClauseTags' comment explains the freeze's rationale from inside specDoc.ts, and Task.clause's comment describes the spec-file tag format from inside taskStore.ts - both describe another module's contract, which CLAUDE.md forbids. undeliveredDoneRefusal's tail and stampClauseIds' second sentence each restate a passing test. About 20 comment lines against about 55 new source lines.

title: handoff's Next: walk-back crosses into the previous branch's plan
deliverable: findLatestNextTrailer stops at the branch's merge-base with the base branch, so handoff reports "no Next: trailer yet on this branch" rather than a trailer written for different work. A cold session is told it has nothing to resume, which is true and checkable, instead of being pointed confidently at the wrong task.
evidence: findLatestNextTrailer walks back up to 20 commits for the most recent commit carrying a Next: trailer, with no branch boundary. Hit on this branch: the first commit, 68b0fcb "Created new task", carried no trailer, so the walk crossed the merge commit 9c87fd3 and surfaced its trailer - "Bundle 1, playable combat continuation, npm run tasks -- spec new combat-continuation" - as this branch's next step. That is the plan for a different branch entirely, and handoff printed it under a "(from 9c87fd3, 1 commit back)" note that reads as provenance rather than as a warning. The failure is structural, not a one-off: a fresh branch whose first commit has no trailer will always reach back into whatever the previous branch was planning, and the deeper the walk the more confidently wrong it gets. The 20-commit cap bounds the scan, not the blast radius.

title: audit can record a finding but has no flag to give it evidence
deliverable: A finding recorded by tasks audit can carry evidence, so triage shows what is broken as well as what fixing it would mean. Either --evidence attaches to the open --finding the way --severity and --deliverable already do, or audit refuses a finding with no evidence the same way it refuses one with no deliverable.
evidence: parseAuditArgs routes every --evidence to the clause-scoped map regardless of position, unlike --file which is overloaded by position and attaches to the open --finding. cmdAudit then hardcodes evidence: null on every finding it creates. Hit for real: all five findings from pass 1 of task-system-small-test-fixes-to-get-feet-wet were recorded with a deliverable and no evidence, so tasks triage printed the header "evidence - what is broken:" with nothing under it and the queue could not be triaged from inside the tool. The text had to be recovered from the audit's report afterwards with tasks edit. Note the asymmetry the tool already enforces in the other direction: add and audit both refuse a finding with no --deliverable, on the grounds that a finding must say what fixing it would mean, while evidence - the half that says what is broken - cannot be supplied at all.

title: A new clause inherits the met verdict of a deleted clause whose id it recycles
deliverable: An id retired by deleting its clause is never handed to a different clause, so a clause the deliverable gained after the last audit pass cannot reach the merge gate carrying a verdict recorded for something else.
evidence: Sanctioned path only, no hand-editing of the store or the pass record. Three clauses alpha/beta/gamma; tasks audit --proof 1=met 2=met 3=met stamps [c1][c2][c3]. Replace the [c2] beta line with an untagged bullet, then tasks spec amend to reset the freeze baseline. resolveIds hands the newcomer the lowest unclaimed id, which is the freed 2, so pass 1 proof 2: met now grades a clause no auditor has ever seen. tasks check --merge reports 0 issues with no new audit pass recorded. Both new gate walks pass because the id mapping is still a bijection, and duplicate detection sees nothing. specDoc.test.ts:57 asserts the opposite in its own name, so a new clause never steals an existing one, but only exercises an id a live neighbour holds, never one a graded clause retired.

title: evidence after a finding silently swallows clause evidence and overwrites the finding evidence
deliverable: A clause-shaped --evidence N=... typed after a --finding is either refused or routed to clause N, and a second --evidence on the same finding is refused rather than replacing the first, so nothing an auditor typed is dropped without a word.
evidence: Run in a temp fixture: tasks audit demo-spec --proof 1=met --proof 2=unmet --finding some-bug --severity low --system Runtime --deliverable fix-it --evidence broken-here --evidence 2=the-clause-did-not-hold. Exit 0, no warning. The spec records - proof 2: unmet with no evidence at all, the undelivered task demo-spec-clause-2 carries none, and the finding evidence reads literally 2=the-clause-did-not-hold, the auditor real evidence broken-here having been silently overwritten because the last --evidence wins. --file, the flag this positional overloading was copied from, appends instead of replacing, so the same keystroke loses nothing there.

title: handoff asserts a branch has no plan of its own when the trailer is only past the 20-commit cap
deliverable: The two ways the walk can come back empty are told apart: nothing on the branch at all, versus nothing within the commits scanned, so handoff never states as fact something it did not establish.
evidence: In a throwaway repo: a branch off main whose first commit carries Next: the branch plan, followed by 25 trailerless fixups. tasks handoff prints (no Next: trailer yet on this branch - nothing recorded since it left main), which is false; the branch does carry one, 26 commits back. Before e3b31a9 the same case printed the honest (no Next: trailer found in the last 20 commits), so the cap turned from a claim about the scan into a claim about the branch. Not hypothetical here: git rev-list --count puts the branch this one follows, task-system-v2, at 41 commits and archive/task-system-v1 at 24.

title: tasks check crashes on a directory named like a markdown file under docs/specs
deliverable: The per-push spec scan reads only regular files and survives one it cannot parse, so a stray path under docs/specs cannot take down the CI step that exists to validate the task store.
evidence: specIssues calls readFileSync on every readdirSync entry ending in .md without checking it is a file. mkdir docs/specs/archive.md then tasks check exits 1 with an unhandled EISDIR stack trace and prints no task-store result at all. Separately, a non-spec notes.md containing a Deliverable heading, a Proof: line and two [c1] bullets reddens tasks check repo-wide with error: notes tags more than one proof clause. Both measured in a temp specs dir. tasks check runs on every push on both matrix legs of .github/workflows/test.yml. Runtime is not the concern: the whole command is 267ms on the real repository.

title: docs/tasks.jsonl now serialises the same record in two different key orders
deliverable: Every line of the store carries the same field order whichever command wrote it, so a diff shows what changed rather than which code path touched the line.
evidence: loadStore spreads the parsed task then appends clause, so a task written before the field existed gets clause last while cmdAdd, cmdAudit and cmdImport place it after spec. Counted on the current store: 170 lines end with closed then clause, and 8 read spec then clause then requires. That split is most of the 349-line docs/tasks.jsonl diff this branch shows, and it will churn again whenever an old line is next rewritten.

title: handoff walks unscoped when the base ref is missing, restoring the trailer it exists to suppress
deliverable: A merge-base that cannot be computed is distinguished from an empty range, so handoff says it could not find the branch point rather than falling back to the walk this branch removed.
evidence: branchCommitRange returns null for both cases. Measured two ways in throwaway repos: delete the local main after branching, or name the base trunk and leave the default --base-branch main. Both make tasks handoff print Next: OTHER BRANCH PLAN, the previous branch trailer, which is exactly the misdirection clause 5 forbids. A single-branch or shallow clone is the realistic shape; a depth-1 clone was also measured and falls to the same unscoped path. handoff is not run in CI, so the exposure is developer-local.

title: Equipment is an equipped state with authored slots, not a property of carrying an item
evidence: Promoted out of combat-post-chunk7-gaps' 'equipment is inert' clause on 2026-08-01 after the branch chose a real equipped state over carried-is-equipped. An item names its slot the way a recipe names its station; the player holds one item per slot in GameState.equipped; statRange folds an equipped item's stat-bonus tags for PLAYER only; save carries and prunes it; equip/unequip are Directives so a # test can record them.

title: A pool saturated in its rate's direction loses its carried remainder, so where a span is split changes the level
deliverable: resolve() is associative for a pool sitting at its ceiling with a rate pushing into it, so a regenerating foe gives the same level and remainder however the span is cut, from the first instant rather than from the first hit.
evidence: Measured by audit pass 2 on combat-continuation-runtime, span 0-13s, foe stamina regenerating at 7/min: one shot gives level 36516 remainder 40000; split at [0.5,1.2,4,9,13] gives 36458 / 20000. settlePools zeroes the carried remainder whenever the write clamps (effects.ts, the 'clamped' branch), and enterEncounter stands every foe up AT its ceiling, so this is the opening condition of every fight against a regenerating enemy rather than an edge case. Pre-existing for the player — resolve.test.ts picks horizons that leave pools 'mid-range rather than saturated where any two answers agree' — but foes had no rate before this branch, so it became reachable here. enemy-pool.test.ts opens its span at OPENS=2 to step past it.

title: A slot: on # item is validated against nothing, so a typo silently creates a private slot
deliverable: A slot named on # item is checked the way a recipe's station: is, so a near-miss spelling fails at load rather than creating a slot only that item can occupy.
evidence: Found by audit pass 1 on combat-continuation-runtime, then narrowed by pass 2's fix. Three items in one module spelling the slot mainhand, main-hand and mainhnd all load clean and all equip at once, reaching +6 attack with no diagnostic. Pass 1 framed this as 'slot: is like station: in syntax and unlike it in every safety property'; that is no longer true. Slots now match capabilities exactly: the SUPPLY side is unvalidated in both cases (# entity stations: oven is checked against nothing, and neither is # item slot: mainhand), while the DEMAND side is checked in both (# recipe station: against registryCapabilities, and a # test unequip: against registrySlots since 1765d0a). So this finding is really about the supply side of BOTH vocabularies, not about slots specifically: a typo'd stations: is equally undetectable, and fixing one should fix the other. Deciding it needs a declaration site, or a rule that a supplied name no demand ever references is suspect.

title: A deterministic repeating action fires on empty: at segment granularity, not at the instant a result drains the pool
deliverable: A pool drained by a deterministic repeating action's results fires on empty: at the instant it ran out, matching the per-attempt path, and one-shot resolution agrees with split resolution.
evidence: Measured by audit pass 1 on combat-continuation-runtime. A repeating deterministic action with 'on success: drain: 12 vigor' against a vigor pool of 30 whose on empty: carries stop, over a 200s horizon: one-shot banks trophy=200, split at 3s banks trophy=3, split at 10s banks trophy=10. resolveDeterministicSegment applies its whole batch in one applyResults at segment start, so the drain settles at segEnd. drainedAPool closes the same gap for resolveStochasticSegment only. Pre-existing, not introduced by this branch, but the branch fixed the per-attempt half and now names this one on resolve().

title: Unmet deliverable clause 1: Proof clauses can name executable proof targets, and `tasks check --merge` fails when a named target is missing, skipped, or failing. At minimum, support Vitest test-file-plus-test-name targets and a command target for proof that is not a single test.
deliverable: Proof clauses can name executable proof targets, and `tasks check --merge` fails when a named target is missing, skipped, or failing. At minimum, support Vitest test-file-plus-test-name targets and a command target for proof that is not a single test.
evidence: Pass 1 ruled this clause unmet and no pass 2 verdicts were ever written to the spec file, so `done` cannot see a met verdict. Added 2026-08-02: this clause can now never become met on any branch, because task-system-policy-seam c10 names proof-target execution as gone rather than guarded - the clause promises machinery that is being deleted. Same for clause 4 (branch-rename protection, freeze baseline, clause-id retirement) and for clause 8's fifth command (`check --merge`). See superseded-spec-undelivered-deadlock.
reason: Retracted, not discharged. The clause promised executable proof targets and a check --merge that fails on a missing, skipped or failing one. task-system-policy-seam deleted proof-target execution deliberately (fdc706a) and check --merge with it (9629bd4), under c10's 'these are gone, not guarded'. The reasoning is on that spec: a shell-command proof target had produced a CI execution path, a 17-minute gate, and a proof that proved nothing, and removing the capability closed all three findings at once. Targets are still parsed and printed into the auditor prompt; nothing runs them. The promise has no subject left, so it cannot be met and must not sit open as though it could be.

title: Unmet deliverable clause 2: `tasks done` records the commit that closed a task, warns when its store write is uncommitted, and `tasks check` reports task state that exists only in the working tree or points at a closing commit not reachable from `HEAD`.
deliverable: `tasks done` records the commit that closed a task, warns when its store write is uncommitted, and `tasks check` reports task state that exists only in the working tree or points at a closing commit not reachable from `HEAD`.
evidence: Delivered. All three conjuncts verified against the tree on 2026-08-02, not read off the clause. (1) 'tasks done records the commit that closed a task': closedCommit is a live store field carried by 28 records; done x --commit HEAD stored 354be577. (2) 'warns when its store write is uncommitted': dirtyStoreIssue at scripts/tasks.ts:200, three tests assert the message. (3) 'reports task state that exists only in the working tree, or points at a closing commit not reachable from HEAD': both are doctor issues, scripts/tasks.ts:230 and :546. The clause names tasks check for the third, which is now doctor - the same scan under the name it took in 4d0e892.

title: Unmet deliverable clause 4: Spec identity and proof identity cannot be changed accidentally: a branch rename cannot make the merge gate not-applicable while open members exist, a never-amended spec has an opening freeze baseline, top-level proof clauses are the only clauses that receive ids, and a retired clause id is never reused for a new clause that has not been audited.
deliverable: Spec identity and proof identity cannot be changed accidentally: a branch rename cannot make the merge gate not-applicable while open members exist, a never-amended spec has an opening freeze baseline, top-level proof clauses are the only clauses that receive ids, and a retired clause id is never reused for a new clause that has not been audited.
evidence: Three of four sub-properties are mutation-proven, but the freeze-baseline promise is false by default (3 of 4 shipped specs have no `## Baseline`) and dropping it entirely leaves the suite green, and clause-id retirement is enforced only against auto-assignment, not a hand-written `[cN]`.
reason: Retracted, not discharged. The clause promised that a branch rename cannot make the merge gate not-applicable while open members exist, and that a never-amended spec has an opening freeze baseline. Both mechanisms are gone: the merge gate under c10, the deliverable freeze and its baselines in the same clause, and spec amend with its ## Amendments sections. Verified absent - git grep over scripts/ finds no mergeGate, freeze, baseline or amendment machinery. Its third conjunct, that top-level proof clauses are the only clauses receiving ids, survives and is covered by specDoc's own tests.

title: Unmet deliverable clause 5: The auditor path is explicit and repeatable: `tasks audit-prompt <spec>` prints a recommended auditor prompt containing the diff range, proof clauses, member tasks, relevant files, proof targets, required commands, and a mutation testing instruction for pure logic/API proofs.
deliverable: The auditor path is explicit and repeatable: `tasks audit-prompt <spec>` prints a recommended auditor prompt containing the diff range, proof clauses, member tasks, relevant files, proof targets, required commands, and a mutation testing instruction for pure logic/API proofs.
evidence: Delivered. tasks audit-prompt <spec> exists and prints every element the clause enumerates - diff range, proof clauses, member tasks, relevant files, proof targets, required commands, and a mutation-testing instruction for pure logic. Verified by running it against this spec on 2026-08-02: 32 matching lines across the seven required headings. It was used to commission passes 3 and 5 of this repository's own audits, which is the repeatability the clause was asking for.

title: Unmet deliverable clause 8: The testing and gate cost is paid where it buys reliability: most `scripts/tasks.test.ts` command-semantics cases run in-process through exported `run(argv)`, only subprocess/Git-history smoke cases stay out-of-process, `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` are enabled, and `npm test`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run layer-check`, `npm run tasks -- check`, and `npm run tasks -- check --merge --spec task-system-real-world-friction-spec` pass.
deliverable: The testing and gate cost is paid where it buys reliability: most `scripts/tasks.test.ts` command-semantics cases run in-process through exported `run(argv)`, only subprocess/Git-history smoke cases stay out-of-process, `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` are enabled, and `npm test`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run layer-check`, `npm run tasks -- check`, and `npm run tasks -- check --merge --spec task-system-real-world-friction-spec` pass.
evidence: Split, and closed on the substance. Delivered and verified 2026-08-02: most command-semantics cases run in-process through the exported run(argv) (runInProcess in scripts/tasks.test.ts, with subprocess reserved for audit and triage, which need real stdin and a real process); noUnusedLocals and noUnusedParameters are both true in tsconfig.json and have caught five real defects including a test that computed two values and asserted neither; npm test is 52s at 942 tests, well inside the five-minute budget, against the 88s that prompted the clause. Retracted in one conjunct: the clause also required npm run tasks -- check and check --merge to pass, and neither command exists - check became doctor in 4d0e892 and check --merge was deleted under task-system-policy-seam's c10. doctor and every other PR gate pass, measured at close: tsc 3s, layer-check 1s, audit-status 11s, doctor 2s. Closing rather than declining because the cost-of-testing promise the clause exists for is met; the deleted commands are two names in its acceptance list, not its subject.

title: `staleAuditIssue` is unsatisfiable by construction: recording an audit pass creates the commit that reddens the gate
deliverable: Pick one semantics and record it in the spec's ## Decisions: keep only the not-an-ancestor refusal (demote the commit count to a warning), exclude spec/store-only commits from the count, or let `tasks audit` accept the closing commit after the fact. Add a test that records an audit, commits it, and asserts `check --merge` goes green.
evidence: Recording an audit pass advances HEAD past the recorded head, permanently firing the ancestor-but-behind refusal across two audit-and-commit cycles in a clean throwaway repo. title: The five undelivered clause tasks of a superseded spec cannot be closed by any command
deliverable: POLICY QUESTION for a human: the store has no way to express that a spec was abandoned. Decide what happens to an undelivered clause task when its spec is superseded, then give the tool that verb. c5 of task-system-policy-seam answers it - drop --because closes any record - and U5 names these five as its proof, so this record is now a live acceptance test for U5 rather than an open question. Until then the five stay open and there is no non-falsifying exit.
evidence: Found while reconciling U1. Re-verified route by route on 2026-08-02, each refusing differently: decline gives 'is undelivered and cannot be declined'; done gives 'is undelivered and proof clause N is not met in the latest audit pass (pass 1)'; spec done --defer-open does not defer them at all but errors 'not done - neither done nor declined' naming all five; spec remove gives 'undelivered task(s) cannot be removed from a spec'; drop does not exist yet. Confirmed why done can never succeed: only pass 1 is recorded in the spec file and it rules clauses 1, 2, 4, 5 and 8 unmet - exactly these five - and pass 2's verdicts were never written. Two things make this worse than when it was filed. First, three of the five now describe machinery task-system-policy-seam deletes, so they can never become met on any branch: clause 1 is proof targets and check --merge, clause 4 is branch-rename protection plus the freeze baseline plus clause-id retirement, and clause 8's fifth required command is check --merge. Second, start and stop accept an undelivered task and edit does too, so the record can be claimed and annotated but not closed - the tool's only writes on it are the ones that change nothing about its being stuck. Re-run against the post-deletion tree at f0936dc on clause-1, verbatim, store confirmed unchanged after each: 'tasks decline <id> --reason ...' exits 1 with 'error: <id> is undelivered and cannot be declined' (scripts/tasks.ts:769); 'tasks spec remove task-system-real-world-friction-spec <id>' exits 1 with 'error: undelivered task(s) cannot be removed from a spec: <id>' (:989); 'tasks done <id> --commit HEAD' exits 1 with 'error: <id> is undelivered and proof clause 1 is not met in the latest audit pass (pass 1)' (:696); 'tasks drop <id> --because ...' exits 1 with 'unknown command: drop' (:1843). spec done --defer-open was not re-run: it writes across every member of the superseded spec and its refusal is already recorded, so re-measuring it risks a partial write for no new information. The deletions also split the five, which were previously treated as one shape. Three are unachievable on any branch because their subject is gone: clause 1 names proof-target execution and check --merge, clause 4 names the merge gate and the freeze baseline, clause 8's fifth required command is check --merge. The other two are not - every element clause 2 names is in the tree (done records closedCommit at :747, dirtyStoreIssue warns on an uncommitted write, workingTreeOnlyIssues reports working-tree-only state, closedCommitIssues at :302 reports an unreachable closing commit), and every element clause 5 names is printed by audit-prompt at :1173-1205. Those two are stuck only because pass 1 graded them unmet and pass 2's verdicts were never written to the superseded spec file. Recording that pass is not this sweep's to do - a verdict is an auditor's assertion, and writing one to clear a deadlock is the exact fabrication the ledger exists to prevent - but it means c5's drop is the only route for three of the five, not five of five.
reason: closed by U3, not by U5: c2's guard removal made decline --reason work on an undelivered clause task. Verified 2026-08-02 against a scratch copy of the live store on task-system-real-world-friction-spec-clause-1, which declined cleanly and reported 'declining it abandons the clause, it does not discharge it'. The deadlock was never a missing verb, so the drop --because that c5 originally specified is cut rather than built.

evidence: Root cause is broader than first filed. cmdAdd:591 hard-codes a finding's spec to null, so 'tasks add --kind finding --spec X' ACCEPTS the flag, reports success, and drops it — no diagnostic. cmdAudit:1880 does the same, keeping provenance only in source.spec, while cmdAudit:1853 gives an undelivered clause task a real spec. Consequences seen twice on this branch: 36 of 41 inherited records were invisible to list --spec and next, and my own measurement pass wrote 'the spec's premise is wrong by roughly 3x' into a planning document workers were told to trust. A worker re-pointing records hit it again and had to use spec add as a second step. There is also no non-interactive path from 'an agent found something' to 'it is in the branch's queue' — triage is a global interactive walk with no targeted form. This is c9's subject arriving from the side c9 originally did not name: the flag is recognised, understood, then silently discarded, which is worse than refusing it. How to apply: one recorded fact answers which spec a record belongs to; a recognised flag either takes effect or is refused. Re-pointed at f0936dc, where the old :1853/:1880 had run past the end of a file U2 shortened to 1875 lines. cmdAdd's hard-code is scripts/tasks.ts:370, cmdAudit's finding is :1622, and the undelivered clause task that does get a real spec is :1591. title: a closed record cannot be reopened, so a closure made against work that has not happened is unrecoverable
deliverable: Give a closed record a route back to open. c2 forbids refusing a write for a semantic reason and start's refusal is exactly that: the record's state disagrees with the caller, so the tool declines rather than recording what the caller asserted. Whether the verb is start accepting a closed record or a separate reopen is U3's to choose; what c2 requires is that one of them works.
evidence: Measured on a scratch copy of the store at f0936dc, so nothing was mutated: 'tasks start pass2-c-m3 --store <copy>' exits 1 with 'error: pass2-c-m3 is declined, not open' (scripts/tasks.ts:639), and 'tasks stop' exits 1 with 'error: pass2-c-m3 is declined, not in-progress' (:672). No other verb moves a record out of done or declined; the dispatch table has no reopen. This is not hypothetical on this branch. Twenty records were declined across 9637c24 and 44b9c1e, every one of them before a single deletion had landed, with reasons written as predictions. Thirteen were re-checked against the tree at f0936dc and eleven hold outright. Two do not: pass2-c-m3 and tasks-check-reports-freeze-warnings-for-specs-belonging-to-o each route a residual to doctor, and U3 has not run - pass2-c-m3 subject is live at scripts/tasks.ts:133 today. That ratio is the problem rather than the exception: closing ahead of the work is cheap and usually right, so it keeps happening, and the times it is wrong the store has no way to take it back. The decision pass2-c-m3 carried was re-homed into policy-seam-u3's evidence for exactly this reason - it was the only move available.

title: a record's file:line reference rots silently when lines move inside a surviving file
deliverable: We need to make sure that this task isn't stale.
evidence: Found by the post-U2 sweep, 2026-08-02. checkStore warns when a task's files path does not exist, so a DELETED FILE is caught. Nothing catches 264 deleted lines inside a SURVIVING file: every reference below them shifts and keeps resolving, now addressing unrelated code. Eight live records were pointing at the wrong thing after U2 and two had run past EOF, none warned. Concretely: pass2-c-h1's tasks.ts:172 was mergeGateSpecCandidates and now addresses something else; A-H1's tasks.ts:937 was cmdDone's guard and now lands on cmdSpecDone. Why this is the same class CLAUDE.md forbids: a line number in the store is a second copy of a fact owned by the source file, kept in sync by hand, and it fails silently rather than loudly — the exact polarity this spec exists to invert. How to apply: prefer a symbol or path to a line, or have doctor verify that a cited line still contains what the record says it does. Do not add a gate; this is a doctor check.

title: an extra positional argument is silently discarded, which is c9's promise broken through the door c9 did not name

The consequence is the founding defect's shape exactly — a confident wrong answer with no signal — and here it cost a recorded note that a reader would never know was missing. Pass 5 graded the original wording unmet and was right to: it read 'No recorded fact and no refusal is derived from git ... git is referenced as evidence by sha', while c11 requires every event to name its branch, which resolveConfig defaults from git.branch(). A branch name is not a sha, so no implementation satisfied both. Measured before amending, by enumerating all 14 git call sites in tasks.ts: exactly four values reach storage - event.head, closedCommit, and an audit pass's base/head are all shas and were always permitted; event.branch was the only non-sha, and it records where a write happened rather than anything about the task. c8 now prohibits refusals and facts about the work, and permits an inferred default argument that is provenance. The amendment's reasoning is an event against the spec rather than prose in it, which is what c10 requires. The substance pass 5 verified is untouched: every git-derived refusal about the work is gone.

title: Unmet deliverable clause 16: The end-to-end workflow every agent follows is written down in one live document, separate from any branch's spec, and CLAUDE.md points at it.
deliverable: The end-to-end workflow every agent follows is written down in one live document, separate from any branch's spec, and CLAUDE.md points at it. A branch spec is a promise made at a moment and is history once merged; a workflow description must never stop changing, and the two cannot be one file. ### This spec widened on 2026-08-02, and by how much c13–c16 were not in the deliverable this branch opened with. They were added after research into orchestration literature identified the gap the ledger did not close: the store recorded what happened and had no way to express what a worker was *allowed* to do, which is the only thing that makes duplication decidable before two diffs collide. The polarity flip (c1–c12) is a precondition for it — every one of c14's findings is a report, and would have been a refusal under the design this branch replaced. Recorded here rather than left implicit because an audit that finds unrecorded scope is right to, and because the widening is the interesting part: the ledger was necessary and was not sufficient.
evidence: Closed 2026-08-02. Pass 5 graded c16 unmet on content, not structure: docs/workflow.md section 6 asserted 'an audit cannot create work' while an unmet clause creates an open high-severity undelivered spec member that next hands out with no triage (reproduced independently), and the doc omitted the event log entirely. `--round-trip` blames the wrong module when the universe contains a `# remove`
evidence:
`scripts/probe.ts:150-157`. The reload is `[...others, printed]`, where `others` are the *original*
sources. The printed module is serialized from the merged registry, so every other module's edits are
already baked in — and then those modules load again and replay their edits on top. Idempotent edits
survive that; `# remove` does not, because `registry.ts:594` throws when a removal names nothing
loaded.

Demonstrated. `base.dsl` declares `item rope` and `item bread`; `cut.dsl` is `# remove item.base.rope`:

```
base: its serialization does not load
  cut [cut] resolve: # remove item.base.rope names an unknown item: base.rope
cut: its serialization loads to a different registry
  items: added base.rope
```

`base`'s serialization is fine. The tool reports it as broken, in the exact words c4 reserves for a
serializer defect, on the branch's headline use case. Not a regression — `squash-local-changes.ts`
had the same reload-with-replay shape before this branch — but the new tool's claim is what fails.

title: `parseVitestTally` reads stdout+stderr and takes the last match, so a stderr line can invert the verdict

`scripts/mutate.ts:86-92` and `:255-259`. `runTests` builds `raw = stdout + stderr`, which destroys
ordering, and `parseVitestTally` takes the last `Tests` line. In vitest 4.1.9 the summary is on
stdout while the Failed Tests block and test-emitted output go to stderr, so any stderr line of that
shape wins.

Demonstrated on real captured bytes from a test that `console.error`s a tally-shaped line and fails:

```
stdout+stderr (what runTests builds): {"failed":0,"total":999}
stdout alone (the truth)            : {"failed":1,"total":2}
```

`0 failed of 999` reads SURVIVED where the truth is KILLED; a `Tests 3 failed` decoy inverts it the
other way. Latent — nothing in the current suite prints such a line — but it is a silent inversion of
the tool's only output, and it compounds with M3, which discards the evidence that would contradict
it. The fix is to parse stdout only.

title: the two fixes pass 1 rated HIGH are both unfalsifiable by the suite
evidence:
Measured with `npm run mutate`, whole-suite scope, baseline 1113, and independently reproduced:

```
h1-reload-originals        SURVIVED  0 failed of 1113  [whole suite]
h2-tally-reads-stderr      SURVIVED  0 failed of 1113  [whole suite]
probe-parsed-truncated     SURVIVED  0 failed of 1113  [whole suite]
registry-parsed-unordered  SURVIVED  0 failed of 1113  [whole suite]
```

`scripts/mutate.ts:353` is the H2 fix, `parseVitestTally(stdout)`. Reverting it to
`parseVitestTally(\`${stdout}${stderr}\`)` — the pass-1 defect verbatim — kills nothing, because
`runTests` is a `const` inside `main()` and only the `RunTests` *type* is exported. No test can reach
it. The fix is guarded by a three-line comment and nothing else.

`src/content/roundTrip.ts:42` is the H1 fix, `reload(sources)` where `sources` are the
serializations. Changing the argument to `reload(modules.map((each) => each.source))` kills nothing,
and that mutant makes `--round-trip` **always report clean** — the tool's entire purpose becomes
inert, invisibly. All five `roundTripUniverse` tests supply their own `reload` closure and assert on
what the closure does to the text it receives; not one asserts anything about the argument it was
handed. Commit `a7462c0` also deleted the only probe test that asserted `--round-trip` can report a
failure and replaced it with one asserting the opposite, so every remaining probe round-trip test
asserts `ok: true`.

This is the failure `docs/workflow.md` §6 exists to prevent, occurring in the branch that ships the
tool for preventing it. The branch author's report that "all ten fixes died" does not reproduce for
these two: the mutations run were of the adjacent pure functions — `parseVitestTally` itself, and a
reload argument that added a duplicate `# info` and so failed the load for an incidental reason —
rather than of the decision each finding was about.

Both are about five lines to pin. H2 wants `runTests` split so the stream choice is data:
`export function tallyOf(streams: { stdout: string; stderr: string }): TestRun`, which is the

test's reload closure to capture the sources it receives and assert they equal `result.sources`, plus

title: a truncated journal permanently wedges `mutate`
evidence:
`scripts/mutate.ts:309-310`. `JSON.parse(readFileSync(JOURNAL, 'utf8'))` is unguarded, and the
journal is written by one non-atomic `writeFileSync` carrying the full pre-mutation bytes of every
target — a wide window. A run killed during that write leaves a half-written journal, and every
subsequent run then dies before reading the manifest, before recovering anything, before restoring
anything:

```
SyntaxError: Unterminated string in JSON at position 69
    at main (scripts/mutate.ts:310:26)
journal still there? YES
```

The stack trace names `mutate.ts`, not the journal path, so the only escape — deleting an
undocumented file in `os.tmpdir()` — is not discoverable from the error. The recovery mechanism
becomes an unconditional crash in exactly the scenario it was added for.

title: journal recovery writes one checkout's bytes into another, bypassing the containment fix
evidence:
`scripts/mutate.ts:236, 252-263, 315`. `JOURNAL` is one fixed path per machine carrying no record of
which repository root it was captured from. `recoverFrom` resolves every key against *this* process's
`repoRoot` and writes with no `escapesRoot` check — that fix is applied to `mutations` and not to
journal keys. Demonstrated with a dead-pid journal naming one relative and one absolute path:

```
recovered 2 file(s): zz-journal-victim.txt, C:/…/scratchpad/outside-victim.txt
--- zz-journal-victim.txt ---   BYTES FROM ANOTHER CHECKOUT
--- outside-victim.txt ---      WRITTEN OUTSIDE THE REPO ROOT
```

Two worktrees of this repo on one machine: a run in A is killed, and the next run in B silently
overwrites B's files with A's bytes and calls it recovery. Not hypothetical — `.claude/worktrees/` is
in vitest's exclude list because worktree-isolated agents are how this repo parallelises. Key the
journal filename by a hash of `repoRoot`, store the root inside it and refuse a mismatch, and run
`escapesRoot` over journal keys before writing.

title: the ordering contract on the new public `UniverseLoadResult.parsed` is prose only

title: the baseline pass runs before the manifest is validated
evidence:
`scripts/mutate.ts:358-368` against `:370`. `refuse()` is pure and needs only `files.read`, but runs
inside `runMutations` after N full test runs. A one-character indentation error in a `find` cost four
baseline runs, about 90 seconds, and then `applied nothing — the manifest was refused`. c7's
guarantee still holds; the ordering is backwards for cost.

title: the report cannot say a verdict had no baseline
evidence:
`scripts/mutate.ts:194, 365-367`. If a baseline run throws, `shortfall` is `undefined` and
`formatReport` renders nothing — byte-identical to a verdict that had a baseline and no shortfall.
The only notice is one stderr line during the preamble, and the report is on stdout, which is what
gets pasted into an audit. This is c8's own argument: a `SURVIVED` measured without a baseline is a
weaker claim, and the report does not distinguish them.

title: the journal is not a lock; two runs can both start
evidence:
`scripts/mutate.ts:309` to `:330`. Between the `existsSync` check and the write sit the recovery
branch and the pre-read of every target. Two runs launched together both see no journal, both
proceed, the second clobbers the first's journal — destroying its only recoverable copy — and both
mutate one tree. `writeFileSync(JOURNAL, …, { flag: 'wx' })` with `EEXIST` as the busy path makes it a
real lock. Reasoned from the code, not raced.

title: `--show`'s vocabulary is split between DSL kinds and registry map names
evidence:
`scripts/probe.ts:25, 94`. `--show variable.travel-seconds-per-unit` is refused;
`--show variables.travel-seconds-per-unit` works. The accepted list is nine singular authoring kinds
and three plural internal map names in one undifferentiated row. `# variable` is what the DSL says,
so the natural guess is the wrong one. Pass 1's M5 is half-closed: the records are reachable, under a
name the author never types.

title: `restoreFailures` is unproven
evidence:
Deleting `|| restoreFailures.has(file)` (`mutate.ts:179`) SURVIVED at whole-suite scope, because the
M2 test's throwing write also leaves the bytes wrong and the byte-compare catches it alone. Pinning
it needs a store whose write throws *after* landing the bytes; otherwise the condition is either dead
or a guard against a case nobody has named.

title: pid reuse wedges the busy check
evidence:
`journalVerdict` (`:247-250`) compares only `pid`, while `startedAt` is recorded and never used. A
recycled pid reads as permanently busy. The message tells the user to delete the journal, so it
degrades to a documented manual step, but comparing `startedAt` would close it for free.

title: `UniverseRoundTrip.printed` carries a second meaning on an inherited field
evidence:
`roundTrip.ts:41`. It is a `// --- name ---`-labelled concatenation of every module, and is not
loadable — multiple `# info` gives "declares # info more than once" — yet it inherits the field name
and type from `RoundTrip.printed`, where `printed` is the reloadable text. Computed on every call;
probe never reads it; one test asserts on it.

title: `alive()` treats EPERM as dead
evidence:
`:300-307`. A `process.kill(pid, 0)` EPERM is treated the same as ESRCH, so a journal held by a live
process owned by another user reads as dead and gets recovered.

title: the journal is plaintext source in a world-known path
evidence:
`:372`. Full source bytes in `os.tmpdir()`, left there whenever `unrestored` is non-empty. Per-user
tmp on Windows makes this minor, but it is uncommitted work at a predictable location.

title: the corpus-count test forces a hand-edit per archived audit

`scripts/lib/auditImport.test.ts:100,110` pins exact finding counts across `docs/audits/`.
Pre-existing, not this branch's doing, but this branch is the first to pay it twice, and CLAUDE.md

title: the lazy baseline is measured on the mutated tree
evidence:
`scripts/mutate.ts:167-172, 185-187, 461-477`. `measure` calls `baselineFor`, and `measure` is called
from `runMutations` *after* `files.write(mutation.file, applyTo(...))`. Both the narrow and the wide
baseline are therefore taken with the mutant on disk. Instrumented:

```
narrow saw MUTANT
  baselineFor(narrow) ->
narrow saw MUTANT
whole  saw MUTANT
  baselineFor(whole) ->
whole  saw MUTANT

verdict: SURVIVED | total: 25 | shortfall: undefined
Truth: 40 tests run unmutated, 25 mutated. The shortfall is 15.
```

End to end, breaking `roundTrip.ts` so one file cannot collect:
`breaks-collection-of-one-file KILLED 3 failed of 1086` against a suite of 1153 — 67 tests silently
stopped running and the row says nothing, because the whole-suite baseline was itself measured at
1086. The poisoned value is memoised and reused by every later mutation in that scope. The usage text
still claims "Each distinct test scope is run once unmutated first", which is no longer true.

This is the class of bug the shortfall exists to catch, and it is reachable: a mutation that does not
compile produces `Tests 0 failed` at narrow scope, because vitest 4 counts a collection failure on
the `Test Files` line only, which `parseVitestTally` never reads. `total === 0` does not fire, so the
verdict is SURVIVED, and the one remaining guard — the test-count drop — is exactly what the poisoned
baseline suppresses. The tool then asserts a coverage gap that does not exist. Two fixes are needed:
take the baseline before the write, and read `Test Files ... failed` so an uncollectable file is an
ERROR rather than a verdict.

title: `--round-trip=module` reintroduces the defect commit 7b16910 fixed
evidence:
`scripts/probe.ts:123-140`. `canSerialize` has exactly one call site, in the universe path, and the
guard was not carried into the module path.

```
$ npm run probe -- snippet.dsl --round-trip=module
snippet: publishing this module alone would not preserve the universe
  items: missing rock                                            <- exit 1

$ npm run probe -- snippet.dsl --round-trip
not round-tripped: snippet declare no # info ...                 <- exit 0
```

`7b16910`'s commit body, verbatim: "`--round-trip` on a source with no `# info` reported
`items: missing rock`, which reads as a serializer defect. It is not." The new mode reports exactly
that for the same input. The principle that commit named — a check that could not run is not a check
that failed — is violated in the new path, and no module-mode test covers a source without `# info`.

title: one pre-existing red test turns every escalated verdict into a false KILLED
evidence:
`scripts/mutate.ts:156, 470`. The verdict compares `run.failed > 0` against zero rather than against
the baseline's failure count, and `baselineFor` records `.total` only. This existed before c14 but was
rare, because the whole suite had to be chosen deliberately. Now narrow scopes are the recommended
default and every survivor is pushed into the full suite, where any unrelated red test lives. A false
SURVIVED gets investigated; a false KILLED closes the question and records coverage that is not there.
The whole-suite baseline already runs unmutated — recording its `failed` and refusing to escalate on a
red tree costs one field.

title: `escalatedFrom` is lost when the escalated run throws
evidence:
`scripts/mutate.ts:188-189`. `runMutations`'s catch rebuilds the result from `scopeOf(mutation)` with
no knowledge of what `measure` had established, so the reader sees an ERROR against the narrow scope
and cannot tell the mutation survived that scope and then the whole-suite run blew up.

title: a refused manifest leaks the journal lock
evidence:
`scripts/mutate.ts:456-459` exits without `rmSync(JOURNAL)`. Demonstrated: after a refusal the journal
survives, and the next run reports "a journal from an interrupted run was found". Three consequences —
the full bytes of every target sit in tmpdir indefinitely; the one message that should mean "check
your tree" fires routinely after every typo'd manifest, which is how a real warning becomes invisible;
and a second run started while the first is alive refuses with "another mutate run is holding this
tree" for a lock held by nothing.

title: the narrow verdict's shortfall is discarded by escalation
evidence:
`scripts/mutate.ts:170-171` returns `{...wide, escalatedFrom}`, replacing everything measured narrowly.
The disagreement between narrow and wide is the most informative thing an escalation produces — it
names the file missing a test — and the row keeps only the wide half.

title: module mode's diagnostic relocates the pass-1 blame rather than resolving it
